name: Three Forks / Noontootla Creek (Benton MacKaye & Appalachian Trail junction)

camps.name: Backcountry camp ~0.30 mi up the real AT/Benton MacKaye Trail from the FS-58 trailhead (exact tent pad unverified — see notes)

pan_reaches.name: Noontootla Creek corridor near the backcountry camp (~0.30 mi up-trail)

creek: Noontootla Creek (Stover, Chester, Long Creeks confluence)
gold_evidence: 1911 USFS land purchase named 'Rock Creek and Noontootly Creek area' tract (Gennett brothers, Fannin/Gilmer/Lumpkin/Union); thediggings.com Fannin County gold index lists Hackney Placer and Noontootly Creek mining.
land_status: Chattahoochee NF, Blue Ridge Ranger District, non-Wilderness. Legality of hand panning on this exact reach not confirmed in writing by USFS; call district before trip.
hazards: Creek crossings; Long Creek Falls nearby (slick rock, avoid panning at falls); shared corridor with AT thru-hikers; black bear country.
pressure: Three Forks itself is a popular car-camp/thru-hiker waypoint; move upstream/downstream for solitude.
coord_source: Trailhead coordinates converted from N34°39.815' W084°11.053' published in N2Backpacking BMT access directions: https://n2backpacking.com/hikes/georgia/benton-mackaye-trail-big-stamp-gap-to-three-forks/

photos.credit: panoramio via Wikimedia Commons, photo at 34.6737,-84.1972 (geosearch near Three Forks)

notes: Top overall pick among the wide-net candidates: strongest creek-specific gold citation, easy grade, established camping, non-Wilderness. Exact hike-in mileage from Three Forks to a private/quiet pan site is unverified. name: Rock Creek dispersed area (Fannin County) — hike upstream from road-end

trailhead.name: Rock Creek Dispersed Area / Rock Creek Road

camps.name: Dispersed site upstream of hatchery/campground cluster (exact site unverified)

pan_reaches.name: Rock Creek upstream of GA DNR Rock Creek hatchery

gold_evidence: Same 1911 Gennett-tract citation as Three Forks explicitly names 'Rock Creek and Noontootly Creek area of Fannin, Gilmer, Lumpkin and Union counties.'
land_status: Chattahoochee NF, part of Blue Ridge WMA (20,900 ac); WMA license/GA Lands Pass may be required for all persons on site — unconfirmed whether this applies to this specific recreation area.
hazards: Firearms deer season (WMA hunt calendar may differ from general NF dates); active fish hatchery nearby, respect boundaries.
pressure: Popular trout-fishing dispersed camping corridor near the road; better solitude moving away from vehicle sites.
coord_source: Campflare listing for Rock Creek Dispersed Area: https://campflare.com/campground/rock-creek-dispersed-area-757
notes: Fundamentally a drive-to dispersed camping road; to be a true backcountry overnight, park at the end of maintained gravel and hike upstream. Distance to a quiet site is unverified.

name: Duncan Ridge / Benton MacKaye Trail at Toccoa River suspension bridge

trailhead.name: Bryson Gap (approximate access point, coordinates unverified)

camps.name: Toccoa River suspension bridge camp cluster (coordinates unverified)

pan_reaches.name: Toccoa River at the Duncan Ridge Trail suspension bridge crossing

gold_evidence: Weak/regional only — no source found naming a specific historic mine or placer directly on the Toccoa River in this drainage; inference from broad Fannin/Union county goldfield context and proximity to the Rock Creek/Noontootly Gennett tract.
land_status: Chattahoochee NF, non-Wilderness (Duncan Ridge NRA corridor).
hazards: 260-ft suspension footbridge crossing (can sway); larger/deeper water than creek candidates.
pressure: Moderately popular DRT/BMT waypoint; some thru-hiker/day-hiker traffic.
coord_source: No coordinates published in sources found for Bryson Gap trailhead or the bridge camp; one-way mileage and elevation from N2Backpacking route description.
notes: Great camping/trail logistics but weakest gold citation of the top four candidates. Needs a CalTopo/Gaia GPS check for real coordinates before use.

name: Amicalola Creek, Dawson Forest WMA (upper NF reaches outside the state park)

trailhead.name: Amicalola River Trails access, GA 53 bridge (exact coordinates unverified)

pan_reaches.name: Amicalola Creek, Dawson Forest WMA Amicalola tract, above/outside Amicalola Falls State Park boundary (unmapped in this pass)

gold_evidence: Strongest of this batch: historic Missing Link Mine (aka Ellsworth Mine, Magic Mine, Baby Placer, Amicalola Mine, Miller Placer) and Nina Head Placer, both named for this creek/area in Dawson County mining records.
land_status: Mixed: Amicalola Falls State Park bans panning; surrounding Dawson Forest WMA (25,500 ac, five tracts incl. an 'Amicalola' tract) is NF/WMA land where standard hand-panning rules should apply. Exact park/WMA boundary along the creek not mapped in this pass — key open question.
hazards: Active WMA hunting land, deer season opens Oct 17; must positively confirm being outside state park boundary before panning.
pressure: Popular for mountain biking/hiking/tubing near GA 53 river access; lower away from road.
coord_source: No precise coordinates found in sources for the GA 53 river-access parking lot or for a specific NF pan reach; general area only.

photos.credit: Wikimedia Commons, geosearch near Amicalola Falls (34.5669,-84.2450) — falls itself is inside the no-panning state park, shown for area context only

notes: Best individual mine citations of any candidate but weakest on route specificity; likely at or beyond the 75-min drive budget. Needs a Dawson Forest WMA office call and a WMA map before use, plus explicit confirmation of the park/WMA boundary.

name: Wildcat Creek headwaters, Rabun County (Wildcat Road, above Lake Burton)

camps.name: Dispersed sites at/above Wildcat Creek Campground #2 Upper (coordinates unverified)

pan_reaches.name: Wildcat Creek, upstream reaches near Wildcat Road dispersed camping

gold_evidence: Rabun County Historical Society documents gold mining on Wildcat Creek on James Stonecypher's land, western shore of Lake Burton, part of a combined $150,000-$250,000 output from Dick's/Moccasin/Wildcat Creek operations countywide.
land_status: Chattahoochee NF, Tallulah Ranger District, non-Wilderness. May require hunting/fishing license or GA Lands Pass for all persons on site per nearby WMA-style signage — unconfirmed whether this exact reach is WMA.
hazards: Firearms season; creek crossings; narrow gravel access road.
pressure: Primitive, less-trafficked relative to the drive-up lower Wildcat Creek Campground #1.
coord_source: No precise coordinates published in sources found for the upper campground or creek reach.
notes: Documented historic gold workings were near the creek's mouth (now near Lake Burton); unconfirmed whether the upstream dispersed-camping reach overlaps gold-bearing gravel. Near the outer edge of the drive-time budget.

name: Moccasin Creek, upper NF reaches above Moccasin Creek State Park

trailhead.name: Not identified in this research pass

pan_reaches.name: Upper Moccasin Creek, NF land above the state park boundary (unmapped)

gold_evidence: Same Rabun County Historical Society source as Wildcat Creek: documented gold mining on Moccasin Creek, James Stonecypher's land, western shore of Lake Burton.
land_status: Lower creek/Lake Burton confluence is inside Moccasin Creek State Park (panning banned); upper NF reaches plausible but no trailhead or FS road identified.
coord_source: No coordinates found for any specific upper-creek access point.
notes: Least trip-ready candidate: real gold citation but no confirmed access point. Not recommended without a follow-up research pass or ranger-district call.
